'''Elon Lindenstrauss''' ({{langx|he|אילון לינדנשטראוס}}; born August 1, 1970) is an Israeli [[mathematician]], and a winner of the 2010 [[Fields Medal]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Israeli wins world's most prestigious math prize|url=https://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3939799,00.html|access-date=19 August 2010|newspaper=ynet|date=19 August 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zimbio.com/pictures/XjS8spYBEzE/Israeli+Mathemetician+Elon+Lindenstrauss+Wins |title=Israeli Mathemetician Elon Lindenstrauss Wins Field Medal&nbsp;— Pictures |publisher=Zimbio |access-date=2010-08-21}}</ref>

Since 2004, he has been a professor at [[Princeton University]]. In 2009, he was appointed as a Professor at the [[Einstein Institute of Mathematics]] at the [[Hebrew University]]. In 2024 he was appointed a permanent faculty member in the School of Mathematics of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/news/three-world-leading-mathematicians-join-ias-faculty |title=Three World-Leading Mathematicians Join IAS Faculty - Press Release &#124; Institute for Advanced Study |date=July 2024 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Lindenstrauss was born into an Israeli-Jewish family with [[German Jews|German Jewish]] origins,  the son of the mathematician [[Joram Lindenstrauss]], the namesake of the [[Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma]], and computer scientist Naomi Lindenstrauss, both professors at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. His sister Ayelet Lindenstrauss is also a mathematician. He attended the [[Hebrew University Secondary School]]. In 1988 he was awarded a bronze medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad.  He enlisted to the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]]'s [[Talpiot program]] and studied at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where he earned his BSc in [[Mathematics]] and [[Physics]] in 1991 and his master's degree in mathematics in 1995. In 1999 he finished his Ph.D., his thesis being "Entropy properties of dynamical systems", under the guidance of Prof. Benjamin Weiss. He was a member at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], then a Szego Assistant Prof. at [[Stanford University]]. From 2003 to 2005, he was a Long Term Prize Fellow at the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]].

==Academic career==
In Fall 2014, he was a Visiting Miller Professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Elon Lindenstrauss|date=17 March 2014 |url=https://simons.berkeley.edu/people/elon-lindenstrauss|publisher=Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing|access-date=24 May 2017}}</ref> Lindenstrauss is an editor for [[Duke Mathematical Journal]] and [[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dukeupress.edu/duke-mathematical-journal|title=Editorial board|website=Duke Mathematical Journal|access-date=16 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.huji.ac.il/~w-jam/board.html|title=Editorial board|website=Journal d'Analyse Mathématique|access-date=16 October 2022}}</ref>

Lindenstrauss works in the area of dynamics, particularly in the area of [[ergodic theory]] and its applications in [[number theory]]. With [[Anatole Katok]] and [[Manfred Einsiedler]], he made progress on the [[Littlewood conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Einsiedler | first1=Manfred | authorlink1=Manfred Einsiedler
| last2=Katok | first2=Anatole | authorlink2=Anatole Katok
| last3=Lindenstrauss | first3=Elon
| title=Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture
| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]
| volume=164
| issue=2
| pages=513–560
| date=2006-09-01
| doi=10.4007/annals.2006.164.513 | doi-access=free
| arxiv=math.DS/0612721 |bibcode=2006math.....12721E
| mr = 2247967 | zbl=1109.22004 | s2cid=613883}}</ref>

In a series of two papers (one co-authored with [[Jean Bourgain]]) he made major progress on [[Peter Sarnak]]'s Arithmetic Quantum Unique Ergodicity conjecture. The proof of the conjecture was completed by [[Kannan Soundararajan]].

Recently with [[Manfred Einsiedler]], [[Philippe Michel (number theorist)|Philippe Michel]] and [[Akshay Venkatesh]], he studied distributions of torus periodic orbits in some arithmetic spaces, generalizing theorems by [[Hermann Minkowski]] and [[Yuri Linnik]].

Together with [[Benjamin Weiss]] he developed and studied systematically the invariant of [[mean dimension]]<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Lindenstrauss | first1 = Elon
| last2 = Weiss | first2 = Benjamin | authorlink2=Benjamin Weiss
| title = Mean topological dimension
| journal = [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| date = 2000-12-01
| issn = 0021-2172
| pages = 1–24
| volume = 115
| issue = 1
| doi = 10.1007/BF02810577 | doi-access=free
| citeseerx = 10.1.1.30.3552}}</ref> introduced in 1999 by [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Mikhail Gromov]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Gromov | first1=Misha | authorlink1=Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov
| title=Topological invariants of dynamical systems and spaces of holomorphic maps: I
| journal=Mathematical Physics, Analysis and Geometry
| volume=2
| issue=4
| pages=323–415
| date=1999
| doi=10.1023/A:1009841100168 | doi-access=
| bibcode=1999MPAG....2..323G | s2cid=117100302}}</ref> In related work he introduced and studied the [[small boundary property]] and stated [[Universal space#Universal spaces in topological dynamics|fundamental conjectures]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1 = Lindenstrauss | first1 = Elon
| title = Mean dimension, small entropy factors and an embedding theorem
| journal = [[Publications Mathématiques de l'Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]]

== Awards and recognition==
*In 1988, Lindenstrauss represented Israel in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] and won a bronze medal.
*During his service in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]], he was awarded the [[Israel Defense Prize]].
*In 2003, he was awarded the [[Salem Prize]] jointly with [[Kannan Soundararajan]].
*In 2004, he was awarded the [[European Mathematical Society]] Prize.
*In 2008, he received the [[Michael Bruno (economist)|Michael Bruno]] Memorial Award.
*In 2009, he was awarded the [[Erdős Prize]].
*In 2009, he received the [[Fermat Prize]].
*In 2010, he became the first Israeli to be awarded the [[Fields Medal]], ''for his results on measure rigidity in [[ergodic theory]], and their applications to [[number theory]]''.<ref>{{cite web| title = Fields Medal – Elon Lindenstrauss, ICM2010 | url = http://www.icm2010.in/imu-prizes/prize-winners-2010/fields-medal-elon-lindenstrauss}}</ref>
